Row.Text: Culture becomes a living field that spreads from your cities tile by tile. A strong, established culture slowly grows its borders beyond the normal city footprint, seeps into open land, and can flip a rival's frontier tiles once your culture there decisively wins, which gives the AI's forward-settling a systemic answer. Growth is slow: borders creep outward over the game and flow back when a culture weakens, and an overwhelming culture reaches farther. A reimagining and extension of the Civ V mod Cultural Diffusion, rebuilt for Civ VII with a deeper cultural-power model and optional Emigration integration. Single-player, with Low/Medium/High intensity and an off switch. Works standalone, and reads diaspora data from the Emigration mod when it is installed. Every rule is explained in the Cultural Diffusion section of the in-game Civilopedia.

How aggressively culture spreads your borders. Low nudges into empty land only; Medium contests rival frontier tiles; High spreads farther and flips faster. Civilopedia: Cultural Diffusion, Options & Presets.
Master switch. When off, borders behave exactly as in the base game. Full rules in the Civilopedia, Cultural Diffusion section.
Cultural Diffusion - claim empty land only
Safety mode. Diffusion claims only unowned frontier plots and never flips a tile owned by another civilization. Civilopedia: Cultural Diffusion, Claiming Tiles.

How deep culture may push into a rival's city. Full downtown ring keeps the ring around their center safe. Center only (default) lets culture take the tiles around the center. None leaves no ring protected. The center itself never changes hands as a tile: it goes only when the whole settlement joins another civilization. Civilopedia: Cultural Diffusion, Claiming Tiles.
Protect city center only (take inner tiles)

On (recommended): culture only claims tiles touching your land, so a rival's territory is taken from the outside in. Off: culture may claim any tile it dominates, including a disconnected pocket inside another civilization. Civilopedia: Cultural Diffusion, Claiming Tiles.

Drive border spread with a civilization's whole cultural power (wonders, culture, influence, happiness, prosperity, traditions) rather than culture per turn alone. A stronger culture pushes its borders farther. Off = the simple settlement-culture model. Civilopedia: Cultural Diffusion, Cultural Strength.

When the Emigration mod is installed, let a frontier tile settled by your people feel your pull, so borders follow diaspora. No effect if Emigration is absent. Requires the rich cultural model. Civilopedia: Cultural Diffusion, With Emigration.
Cultural Diffusion - claim land beside new improvements (+1 ring)

Off by default. When on, finishing a rural improvement near your border also claims the unowned tiles right next to it, one ring past your city's normal reach. When off, your borders grow only from the culture field. Civilopedia: Cultural Diffusion, Claiming Tiles.

Off by default. Tiles your culture claimed can be lost again: if a rival's culture decisively overtakes yours on one, it passes to that rival's nearest city. Tiles your cities gained through normal growth are never affected. Civilopedia: Cultural Diffusion, Borders Recede.
Cultural Diffusion - every civilization gains land by culture

On by default. Other civilizations' borders move by culture too, under the same rules as yours: a rival whose culture decisively leads a tile near your lands takes it, including tiles of yours, and can lose tiles the same way. City-states and independent peoples never gain land this way. You are told when a rival takes one of your tiles. Off = only your borders grow by culture. Civilopedia: Cultural Diffusion, Rival Expansion.
Cultural Diffusion - armies hold the ground they occupy

Off by default. When on, during a war a combat unit that holds an enemy tile for five consecutive turns takes it for its owner, whatever the culture there; leaving resets the count, and city centers and urban districts are never taken this way. The conquered tile is then held against culture for ten turns, though another army can still take it. Other civilizations' armies do the same only when "every civilization gains land by culture" is also on. Civilopedia: Cultural Diffusion, Armies Hold Ground.
Cultural Diffusion - cities carry every culture living in them

On by default. A city produces culture for every people present on its tile, not only its owner's: a captured or mixed city keeps producing its old culture, which contests the land around it, while each turn a small share of that foreign culture converts to the owner's (faster with libraries, universities, museums and, in the Modern age, an ideology). Off = a city produces only its owner's culture. Civilopedia: Cultural Diffusion, Mixed & Captured Cities.
Write detailed per-pass diagnostics to UI.log (for tuning and troubleshooting).

Add a read-only "Cultural Pressure" map lens (and Shift+C hotkey) that shades contested frontier tiles by how close your culture, or a rival's, is to claiming them. Shows information only; it changes nothing about how borders move. Civilopedia: Cultural Diffusion, Cultural Pressure Lens.
Cultural Diffusion: your culture has claimed new territory.
Cultural Diffusion: another civilization has taken one of your tiles.
Cultural Diffusion - whole settlements change hands by culture

On by default. When a neighbor's culture has clearly won a settlement for several turns in a row, the whole settlement joins that civilization: its buildings, districts, wonders and tiles go with it, and you're warned on the first turn. Only between major civilizations at peace; city-states and independent peoples never change hands this way. Civilopedia: Cultural Diffusion, Settlement Flips.
Cultural Diffusion - capitals can change hands by culture
Off by default. When on, a capital can join a neighbor too. It arrives as a town, and the civilization that lost it gets a new capital.
Cultural Diffusion - culture can take a civilization's last settlement
Off by default. When on, a civilization whose last settlement joins a neighbor is defeated.
Cultural Diffusion - grievances when a settlement changes hands

How many grievances the civilization that lost a settlement holds against the one that gained it (30 by default). Their relationship drops by the same amount and recovers over time; the grievances stay.
Cultural Diffusion - turns of clear culture before a settlement changes hands
How many turns in a row a neighbor's culture must clearly hold a settlement before it joins (3 by default). You're warned on the first.
A settlement's people have chosen another civilization.
The people of this settlement have chosen to join another civilization. Cultural Diffusion places it for a moment and removes it once the settlement has changed hands.
The people here have chosen to join another civilization.
